A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ISE research, with matching methods and core experiments. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and evaluation results for instruction following, prompt injection, prompt extraction, harmful requests, over-refusal, and adaptive jailbreaks.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds segment-label ablations, automatically optimized attacks, multi-turn evaluation, and an attention case study.

M1.justification: The learned role embeddings, their addition to token embeddings, and full-parameter supervised fine-tuning remain unchanged. Segment reassignment in Appendix E.6 is an experimental intervention, not a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 extends retained benchmarks to multi-turn MT-Bench, automatically optimized indirect injections, and missing-system-prompt scenarios. These are bounded extensions of test coverage; the underlying training and evaluation corpora remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Structured Query retains the Baseline and Delimiter comparators; Instruction Hierarchy and the added experiments compare Baseline with +ISE. The new tables' 'Instruction Follow' label corresponds to the existing System Follow training condition, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendices E.6–E.8 introduce controlled prompt removal and segment reassignment, iterative GPT-4o attack optimization, and GPT-4o-judged multi-turn evaluation. Appendix B.1 also restricts the previously dataset-wide 50/50 clean/attacked description to samples containing data inputs. This revises the reported construction setting without establishing that training was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic tests of system-prompt and segment-label dependence, an optimized-injection stress test, multi-turn generalization analysis, and an output/attention case study in Appendices E.6–E.9. These substantially extend the existing robustness and diagnostic analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables and figures continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 4–7 add substantial results for hierarchy perturbations, automatic attacks, and multi-turn conversations. For example, Table 6 reports 39.90% Baseline versus 57.21% +ISE robustness for UltraChat; Table 7 reports Instruction Hierarchy multi-turn scores of 4.61 versus 5.40. Previously reported results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The embedding definitions, embedding-summation procedure, and ROUGE-L threshold equation are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear; the added H × D parameter count explains the existing embedding matrix.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same architectural contribution and headline improvements of 15.75%, 18.68%, and 4.1%. Added appendix evidence supports these retained claims. Removing the conclusion's general encouragement for deployment does not materially redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking segment misassignment to instruction confusion and elevated priority for malicious data, discusses multi-turn degradation, and attributes the attention example's resistance to broader attention. These extend the explanatory discussion while retaining the original adaptive-jailbreak and scalability limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies previously missing GPT-4o decomposition and response-generation prompts, examples, exact Alpaca sample breakdowns, and manual-review information. Appendix C.4 supplies the over-refusal judging prompt. Section 9 replaces a future code/data/model-release promise with a reported code release and repository address, substantially expanding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The reference list and Section 7 retain the same works and architectural positioning. Chao et al. (2023), used for the added automatic-attack experiment, was already cited in v1; no substantive novelty repositioning occurs.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the introduction, author/header text, and conclusion; divides Appendix B into subsections; and adds appendix subsections for documentation and analyses. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with data-construction and judging-prompt illustrations, four new experimental tables, and an attack example with attention heatmaps. Figure 29 redisplays Figure 5's robustness results as bar charts. Existing displays are retained and sometimes relocated; the new Table 6 incorrectly carries an MT-Bench caption.

improvement.justification: The added role-label tests, optimized injections, and multi-turn results strengthen validation, while explicit generation and judging prompts improve reproducibility. The gains are bounded by sparse automatic-attack settings and an attention interpretation based on one example; Table 6 also has a misleading caption. The original results and severe adaptive-jailbreak limitation remain unchanged.
